correctness.rationale: Dissipativity forces every real eigenvalue to have an eigenvector of the Hermitian cycle vanishing at the detector. At nonexceptional flux the Fourier energies are distinct and every Fourier vector has detector amplitude n^(-1/2). At zero flux exactly the sine lines of the paired energies are dark; on the bright restriction all eigenvalues are strictly damped, so each dark line is algebraically simple. Independently, the rank-one secular equation is 1+(i gamma/(2n)) sum_l (z-e_l(Phi))^(-1)=0. For the pair near E_k its energies have midpoint E_k+O(Phi^2) and half-splitting of magnitude v_k |Phi|+O(Phi^3), with v_k=2|sin(theta_k)|/n. Writing z as the midpoint plus c Phi^2, the two terms have sum tending to -2c/v_k^2; all other terms have real limits. Equating the imaginary part of the resulting sum to 2n/gamma gives Im c=-n v_k^2/gamma, confirming the author's perturbative width and normalization. At t=s/Phi^2, analytic projections tend to orthogonal sine lines with weights (2/n)sin^2(d theta_k); interference vanishes and the bright complement is uniformly exponentially damped (a fixed lower-half-plane contour suffices even at a defective bright eigenvalue). Integrated distinct slow branches have denominators bounded away from zero by their distinct limiting real energies. Each diagonal term is its exact perturbed weight divided by its decay rate; if the initial dark overlap is zero the weight is O(Phi^2), which proves boundedness rather than merely a zero scaled limit. Thus the coefficient is gamma/4 times the stated trigonometric sum. Fourier orthogonality of the length-r geometric sum gives the full N-cycle sum Nr-r^2; odd-cycle doubling permutes residues and pairing halves the sum, while even-cycle labels run once through the nonzero residues modulo m=n/2. This confirms both parity formulas and all zero-coefficient sites. Finally, tracing the integrated-survival Lyapunov equation gives gamma X_00 equal to the decaying dimension, n away from zero and floor(n/2)+1 on the bright restriction at zero. The frozen numerical script was not executed; the argument is finite-dimensional and analytic.
residual_risks: The small-flux estimates keep n and positive gamma fixed. The survival limit is for s>0 and need not describe the bright transient at s=0.

evidence: Continuous non-Hermitian trapping and unthreaded ring degeneracies are established; the inspected even-ring perturbation in arXiv:0903.3288 varies sink strength rather than flux. The magnetic triangle work measures the target stroboscopically. The half-flux record gives an exact characteristic polynomial for arbitrary flux and a relaxation theorem about a fixed antipodal state near pi.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The spectral machinery and known exceptional phases are genuine coverage. Neither a different monitoring protocol nor a relaxation law near pi is an encompassing theorem for the claimed survival at weak flux. Zero and pi are not gauge equivalent; in particular an even ring has two unpaired bright energies at zero, but none at pi.

evidence: The general Chebyshev determinant in 9c2164f9c4e0 encodes the zero-flux eigenvalue leakage coefficient as well: at x=cos(2 pi k/n), T_n(x)=1, U_{n-1}(x)=0 and dU_{n-1}/dx=-n/sin^2(2 pi k/n). Implicit differentiation with cos(Phi)=1-Phi^2/2+O(Phi^4) gives the same width. Its actual survival theorem uses a wholly dark initial antipode at half flux and equal modal weights.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Do not count an eigenvalue-width recalculation or the overlapping mean limits as independent novelty. A characteristic polynomial gives no initial-state weights; an integrated survival time cannot determine the multiexponential profile. The zero-flux law requires identifying and controlling the projections of an arbitrary site with generally nonzero initial bright weight, the missing bright transient for s>0, and the parity-specific site sums. These are not a parameter substitution into the stated half-flux survival theorem.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Opposite flux orientation does not change the leading even-in-flux singularity. The mixed-state term equals the average of two copies of the r=0,...,m-1 sitewise sequence gamma r(m-r)/4 divided by 2m; matching that average is not a determination of individual site weights or their survival curves. originality.rationale: Credit the uncovered site-resolved zero-flux relaxation profile across both parities and its sitewise mean-time consequences on even rings. The exact odd-ring mean already covers the odd coefficient; the exact even-ring mixed mean covers its site average. The half-flux result gives a closely related relaxation mechanism and a shared exact spectral polynomial, but its antipodal profile at half flux does not contain this zero-flux, arbitrary-site time-dependent statement. The trace identity, static dark-space classification and generic decay mechanism are not original contributions here.
residual_risks: An earlier general rank-one absorption treatment might include a stronger weak-splitting projection law; the checked passages do not establish such coverage.

value.rationale: The full site-resolved transient explains how a static dark probability becomes a set of long-lived absorption channels, rather than merely giving another mean or an ultimate detection probability. The parity-dependent coefficients and exceptional starts distinguish genuine lifetime divergence from a finite discontinuity. Those differences are useful benchmarks for this standard continuous trapping geometry.
residual_risks: Scope is a uniform, fixed finite ring with one Markovian sink; usefulness for jointly large rings or stroboscopic detection is not established.
